name: Example: Finding a Vector That Makes a Set Linearly Dependent
problem:
The set $\{ \mathbf{a_1},\mathbf{a_2} \}$ is linearly dependent. Which of the following vectors could be $\mathbf{a}_2$ if
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044078/assets/2fc772925dd6b793bdcb3a1eca96ea7e7f5fed17425f3500638340e047170c60.png)

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044078/assets/f73258610652de9a656f3c4ed202241c58c98f18391b1393dabe62d92d9bef7d.png)
worked_solution:
We say that two vectors $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_2$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
x_1 \mathbf{v}_1 + x_2 \mathbf{v}_2 = \mathbf{0}
$$

is $x_1 = x_2 = 0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

A set containing *only two* vectors is linearly *dependent* if and only if the two vectors are parallel.

From the given options, the correct answer is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044078/assets/210a5c50467861cdfe48b46f2098212bbf387270b420a05394e318a0e0b48c74.png)
To see why, notice that 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044078/assets/91a29b57d32ed8c8e702f2988f7714ffc343ed6b4707b86b49b708ffad5c8bc8.png)
In other words, the vectors $\mathbf a_1$ and $\mathbf a_2$ are parallel.

To see why this means that $\mathbf a_1$ and $\mathbf a_2$ are linearly dependent, notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{a}_{1}-{a}_{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation

$$
x_1 \mathbf{a}_1  +x_2  \mathbf{a}_2 = \mathbf{0}
$$

has the solution $x_1=\dfrac 1 3$ and $x_2=-1,$ which is different from $x_1=x_2=0.$ Therefore, the set is linearly dependent.
